claims.content: The Customer initiates the browse/search session by accessing the product browse/search capability (e.g., using the Endeca or Endeca-like search and navigation capability to browse inventory, accessing it via the Site Map page, or entering via SEO-optimized landing pages), where the Customer can enter a Product ID (e.g., ABC123) or Customer Email Address, or select search parameters such as Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, Product Type, and Cost Range, and then click 'Go' or 'Find Product' to submit the search.

The primary actor (Customer) wants to browse and search auction inventory items by applying filters and combining search criteria such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, Location, Product ID, Customer Email Address, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, and Cost Range.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The primary actor (Customer) wants to browse and search auction inventory items by applying filters and combining search criteria such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, Location, Product ID, Customer Email Address, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, and Cost Range.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: Customer specifies one or more browse/search filters or criteria and submits the search to obtain matching auction inventory products.
scope_contract.start_boundary: Customer is at the product browse/search interface and has not yet executed the search.
scope_contract.success_boundary: Customer has submitted browse/search criteria and can review the matching auction inventory products.
in_scope_actions: Filter by Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, and Location
Search by Product ID, Customer Email Address, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, Product Type, and Cost Range
variant_dimensions: Which filter or search criterion is used

claims.content: While browsing auction inventory links, if the Customer clicks a link that contains no product (which can happen routinely for collectibles), the system serves a 'no results found' page.

If the submitted search returns no matches, the system displays a 'No Results Found' page that includes: (1) an apology message stating no matches were found; (2) a 'Search Tips' section with 5 suggestions (check typos, remove unnecessary words, try plural/singular forms, use fewer/generic keywords, contact support); and (3) a 'May We Suggest'/'Popular Searches' section containing static lists of popular gemstone and jewelry searches plus search terms/phrases dynamically updated using Omniture data.

Products without an available image are never eligible to appear on product details pages, search results, or catalog pages; this hard filter may cause empty or incomplete result sets even when the submitted criteria match.

If the Customer is not signed in when clicking anywhere within a product module (except the QuickBid button), the system presents a sign-in page; after the Customer completes sign-in, the system delivers them to the Product Details page.

missing_aspects: exit/recovery after the 'No Results Found' page is displayed (e.g., return to search/browse or terminate)
exit/recovery when the image-availability hard filter yields empty or incomplete results (e.g., whether a 'No Results Found' page is shown)

claims.content: The system displays a filtered product list in a table titled 'Search Results'; each row represents a matching auction item and includes a thumbnail image, Product ID (SKU #), Auction ID, Description, Opening Bid, High Bid, Unit Cost, Start time, End time, Duration, Product Type, and Increment.

The search results display data using columns in this default order: 'Action' (checkbox), Item thumbnail image, Product ID (SKU #) with link to SKU History page, Auction ID number, Description, Opening Bid, High Bid, Item Unit Cost, Start time (initially blank), End time (initially blank), Duration (initially blank), Product Type (e.g., Ring, Single Stone), and Increment.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of using the standard browse/search entry point, the Customer may access the browse/search capability via a Site Map page that lists all available Categories (Jewelry, Gemstones, Collectibles, Watches), Product Types (e.g., Rings, Necklaces, Bracelets), and Gemstone Types (e.g., Tanzanite, Diamond, Ruby) as direct links to specific pages or Endeca results pages.

Diverges from Step 1: The Customer may instead enter product browsing via SEO-optimized landing pages focused on specific gemstone types (e.g., 'tanzanite page') or product types (e.g., 'Rings page'), which contain direct links to relevant product categories such as 'all loose tanzanite stones' or 'all tanzanite rings'.

Diverges from Step 2: Before submitting the search, the Customer may choose either 'Items currently online only' or 'All sellable auction inventory' via radio buttons; this selection does not impact the results of the 'Red status' columns.
Diverges from Step 2: The Customer may set combinable radio-button filters to show items with or without images and to show items with or without a valid (sellable) location.
Diverges from Step 5: The Customer may switch between 'List View' and 'Catalog View' display modes for the product results.
Diverges from Step 5: The Customer may sort the product results by 'Current Price: low to high' using a dropdown menu.

Diverges from Step 5: The Customer may group the displayed results using a scrolling list box with options including Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material, Material Purity, Product Group, Brand, Inventory Realm (Red, White), Inventory Aging Bucket, J/G Score, and Ring Size; each grouping option generates corresponding columns in the Results section.
The system has auction inventory data populated and available for the Auctioneer to access.
The Customer browses the auction inventory using the Endeca or Endeca-like search and navigation capability.

The Customer applies one or more filters from the available browse/filter controls, including Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, and Location; where filters are offered as scrolling list boxes (Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone Type, Material Type, Material Purity, Brand), multiple values may be selected using the Control key.

The Customer additionally enters or selects search criteria such as Product ID (wildcards * or % allowed), Customer Email Address, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, Product Type, and low/high Cost Range values.
The Customer combines the selected filters and search criteria and submits the search by clicking the 'Go' button or the 'Find Product' button.

The system displays a table titled 'Search Results' containing rows for matching auction items, with thumbnail images and columns for Action, Image, Product ID, Auction #, Description, Open Bid, High Bid, Unit Cost, Starts, Ends, Duration, Product Type, and Increment.

quality_flags.detail: [trigger_preconditions_coverage] The Trigger has the Customer searching auction inventory, but the only Precondition says the auction inventory data is populated and available for the Auctioneer to access. It does not establish that the Customer-facing browse/search interface has access to that populated inventory before the Trigger. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit evidence for 'browse' in the original 'browse/search interface' is not cited; only search and filtering are supported.))

[altflow_diverge_points] Alternative flow claim 7 (0-based 6) says 'Diverges from Step 4', but it describes grouping displayed results and generating columns in the Results section. That is a post-results display action that belongs after main_flow Step 5, not at the Step 4 submit action. The claim is also unsupported as a customer action: the coverage_state notes the cited evidence is about an internal 'Inventory Performance & Aging Report', not a customer-facing search interface. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (The cited card does not state that the 'Create grouping / event' option creates a grouping/event from selected items.))

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] Main Flow Step 5 ends with a 'Search Results' table whose columns are Action, Image, Product ID, Auction #, Description, Open Bid, High Bid, Unit Cost, Starts, Ends, Duration, Product Type, and Increment. It does not produce the Product Module representation described in Postcondition 1, which contains a countdown timer and QuickBid button. Thus that postcondition is not reachable from the flow as written. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (The cited cards support the Catalog/List View switch and the Product Module display separately, but do not explicitly establish that switching to Catalog View is the trigger for displaying the Product Module list.))

[trigger_preconditions_coverage] The Trigger is initiated by the Customer, but the only precondition says the auction inventory data is available 'for the Auctioneer to access'. That wording does not establish the required customer-facing availability of the inventory data for the Customer's browse/search Trigger, so the precondition is not vertically aligned with the Trigger and primary actor. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (The customer-facing browse/search interface detail is not supported by the cited evidence.))

[trigger_preconditions_coverage] The Trigger requires the Customer to initiate browsing/searching of auction inventory, but the only Precondition states that the inventory data is populated and available for the Auctioneer to access. The Customer-facing browse/search capability therefore lacks a covered prerequisite: the populated inventory must be available to the Customer or to the Customer-facing search service, not merely to the Auctioneer.

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 3 describes the image-availability hard filter and states it may cause empty or incomplete result sets, but it does not specify a clear terminal outcome for that branch. It does not say whether a 'No Results Found' page is shown, a prevention message is displayed, or the Customer is returned to the browse/search flow.

inconsistency_hints: Alternative flow claim 5 (0-based 4) says 'Diverges from Step 4', but switching between List View and Catalog View for product results is a display adjustment made after results are shown in main_flow Step 5, not during the Step 4 submit action.

Alternative flow claim 6 (0-based 5) says 'Diverges from Step 4', but sorting the product results by current price is a results-list manipulation that logically occurs after main_flow Step 5 displays the results, not at the Step 4 submit action.

The Trigger captures only the final submission action (Customer enters criteria and clicks Go/Find Product), whereas the Main Flow is the authoritative browse/filter/search sequence: it starts with browsing (step 1) and only reaches the same submission in step 4. Consequently, Main Flow step 1 cannot continue from the Trigger; the scenario restarts before the Trigger.

Alternative flow claim 7 says 'Diverges from Step 4', but main_flow step 4 is the combine/submit action. The claim describes grouping the displayed results and generating columns in the Results section, which happens after main_flow step 5 displays the results. Thus the divergence point is logically unrelated to the described branch.

Main Flow step 5 only renders a Search Results table with columns Action, Image, Product ID, Auction #, Description, Open Bid, High Bid, Unit Cost, Starts, Ends, Duration, Product Type, and Increment. No step renders the Product Module list required by Postcondition 1, which adds a countdown timer and QuickBid button, so that postcondition is not connected to the displayed result state.
